title: What If You Doubled in Size Every Day? | What If #3
thought_experiment: Labelled thought experiment: a 1.7 m person doubles in height once a day; biology, weight and gravity are ignored. Simplified: heights shown to scale, no body physics.

hook_candidates.text: You double every day. When do you outgrow Earth?
Watch this counter. It stops when you're bigger than Earth.
What if you doubled in size every single day?
Doubling daily, you'd outgrow Earth in twenty-three days.
You're taller than Everest. Tomorrow you'll be twice that.

parts.text: It stops when you're wider than the whole planet.
parts.tts: It stops, when you're wider than the whole planet.

parts.text: Add one body a day instead,
and you've barely left the street.
The day before you outgrow Earth,
you're only about half its size.
One more doubling, on day twenty-three,
parts.tts: One more doubling, on day twenty-three,

parts.text: and you're taller than the planet is wide.
parts.tts: and you're taller, than the planet is wide!

sources: Start height assumed 1.7 m (labelled assumption, a typical adult). Height on day n = 1.7 m x 2^n.
Earth's equatorial diameter 12,756 km (equatorial radius 6,378.137 km): NASA NSSDC Earth Fact Sheet, https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/earthfact.html
Day 23: 1.7 m x 2^23 = 14,260 km > 12,756 km; day 22: 7,130 km = 56% of Earth's diameter ('about half'). Arithmetic.

Mount Everest 8,848.86 m: joint China-Nepal survey announced 8 Dec 2020 (Associated Press via phys.org, https://phys.org/news/2020-12-china-nepal-everest-bit-higher.pdf; Al Jazeera 2020-12-08). Day 12: 6,963 m (below); day 13: 13,926 m (above), i.e. before day 14.
Adding one body (1.7 m) per day instead: 1.7 x 14 = 23.8 m on day 13, roughly a building of six to eight storeys; shown as a picture, not spoken as a number. Arithmetic.
Each doubling adds as much height as all the growth before it plus the start (2^n = 1 + sum of 2^k for k<n): standard geometric series.
Thought experiment only: a real body could not survive this (square-cube law); not claimed in the video.
